reader.requirement: At --std 85 an INITIALIZE whose identifier-1 (any of several, qualified or reference-modified) names a level-66 RENAMES entry, of the THRU form or the single data-name form over an elementary or a group item, must be refused at compile time, while a record beside which a 66 entry is written is initialized normally.
reader.edition-search: grep of InitializeBinder.cs for DialectLevel|CobolVersion|Edition.Year|ConstructRegistry: no match; CheckInitializeTargetRenames reads Place.DenotedItem.Renames only (data.Edition is used as the diagnostic sink, not as a switch). The path consults the edition nowhere, and the 1985 and 2023 rules say the same thing.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness is the positive half (a record with a 66 entry beside it); the refusal of each RENAMES form was not exercised by it

refused (66 RENAMES of an elementary item)

refused (same-named 66 entry under the other record, by qualification)
refused: the reference names the RENAMES entry
REC, REC2 and R3 initialized (spaces / zeros; R31 by 9) — the 66 entries beside them do not reach the rule

reader.notes: The check runs on the resolved place and asks the entry the name denotes (DenotedItem, walking decorators for a reference modification), so every RENAMES form and every qualification is refused and an ordinary record is not. The message cites §2023:14.9.20.3 SR5 at --std 85 (cosmetic).

refuter.evidence: Read InitializeBinder.cs#BindInitializeTarget: the only arm before the RENAMES check is the OCCURS DYNAMIC whole-table arm, which no 1985 program reaches; CheckInitializeTargetRenames asks DenotedItem through decorators. Probes at --std 85: r2fd (66 RENAMES THRU in an FD record, with REPLACING; and a 66 single-name alias in WORKING-STORAGE as the second identifier-1 after a plain record) -> COBOL0835 for FREN and WREN, the plain record W not diagnosed. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.17.3 SR6 'must not contain a RENAMES clause'.
